concept.name: Ladder order
concept.definition: An order strategy that places a series of limit orders at successively higher (for sells) or lower (for buys) price levels, forming a 'ladder' of resting interest across a price range. It is in practice a synonym or close variant of the scale order.
concept.intuition: Like rungs on a ladder, each order sits one step further from the current price, catching the market at progressively better levels.
concept.mechanics: Each rung is an independent limit order with its own size; as price moves through the range, rungs execute in sequence, producing a blended average price. On retail futures/crypto platforms the ladder is often created by one-click bulk placement along the price axis.
concept.formula: Blended price = sum(rung price x rung size) / total filled size.
concept.failure_modes: Fully visible ladders reveal the trader's entire price map and can be traded against; and as with scaling, fills concentrate on the wrong side of trends, so the ladder completes exactly when the position is least wanted.
concept.misconceptions: A ladder is not an exchange order type - it is a placement pattern executed with ordinary limit orders, and it does not guarantee an average price because upper rungs may never fill.
concept.example: Exiting a long, you ladder sell limits at $101, $102, $103, and $104 for a quarter of the position each; a rally to $103 fills three rungs at a $102 average.
